officialDocs.label: Roles in the Selling Partner API

verdict.summary: You can't create an app until Amazon reviews your developer profile (typically one to two weeks; longer, three-stage review for PII roles), and a public app stays capped at 25 seller authorizations until it's listed on the Selling Partner Appstore. Sellers must also reauthorize annually.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Developer profile review 'typically takes one to two weeks'; only after approval can you register an app and self-authorize or use version=beta for draft testing.

timeToProd.assumes: A public seller app with non-PII roles (e.g. inventory, pricing, product listing) listed on the Appstore so any seller can connect; an unlisted app reaches up to 25 sellers right after profile approval, and PII roles add a multi-stage review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Developer profile review (1–2 weeks), then Selling Partner Appstore listing for unlimited seller authorizations.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Profile review time is sourced; Appstore listing review time isn't published, so the upper bound is our estimate.

verdict.cost: None currently. Amazon announced a $1,400/year developer fee plus GET-call usage fees for 2026, then postponed and reportedly cancelled them on May 12, 2026 (not confirmed on an Amazon page we could open).

prerequisites.item: A Solution Provider Portal account (or Seller Central professional account for private seller apps), registered by the primary account user
prerequisites.why: Developer registration happens there and must be done by the primary account user; individual selling accounts aren't eligible for private seller apps.

prerequisites.item: Security control answers written by your security/technical team
prerequisites.why: The profile application asks security control questions that must reflect how you implement the Acceptable Use Policy, Data Protection Policy and Solution Provider Portal Agreement; keep it under 500 words of original text.

prerequisites.item: A public website meeting Amazon's website guidelines
prerequisites.why: Public developers and service providers must meet the website guidelines.

prerequisites.item: Registered HTTPS login and redirect URIs
prerequisites.why: Amazon only sends authorization responses to registered redirect URIs, and the token exchange's redirect_uri must match.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: HTTPS is our assumption from Amazon's security policies; the page says registered URIs.

scopeTiers.impact: Granted via developer profile review. Covers most catalog, inventory, pricing and non-PII order data an agent needs.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Role names are from Amazon's roles page; SP-API uses roles instead of OAuth scope strings.

scopeTiers.impact: Three-stage review: business review, security review, and a technical review meeting with an Amazon solution architect. Calls also need a Restricted Data Token.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Stages are sourced; Amazon gives no durations, so the time is our estimate.

scopeTiers.impact: Up to 25 seller OAuth authorizations (vendors unlimited) plus 10 self-authorizations for testing.
Removes the 25-seller cap: unlimited OAuth authorizations.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Listing review time is not published.

steps.title: Create a Solution Provider Portal account
steps.detail: Sign in as the primary account user and start developer registration.

steps.title: Choose roles
steps.detail: Map the agent's operations to roles and avoid restricted PII roles unless essential, since they trigger a longer three-stage review.

steps.title: Draft the developer profile and security answers
steps.detail: Write an original use-case description under 500 words and draft security-control answers for your team to verify against the Data Protection Policy.

steps.title: Submit the developer profile
steps.detail: Have the technical team confirm the security answers, then submit.

steps.title: Developer profile review
steps.detail: Amazon reviews business requirements and security measures; PII roles add business, security and technical (solution architect) reviews.

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: Create a public app with the approved roles, OAuth login URI and redirect URI; copy the LWA client ID and secret.

steps.title: Implement website authorization
steps.detail: Send sellers to {Seller Central URL}/apps/authorize/consent?application_id=...&state=... (add version=beta for a draft app). Validate state on the redirect page (Referrer-Policy: no-referrer) and exchange spapi_oauth_code within 5 minutes at https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token.

steps.title: Test with your own seller account
steps.detail: Authorize the draft app with version=beta using one of your 10 self-authorizations.

steps.title: Onboard up to 25 sellers unlisted
steps.detail: Publish the app unlisted and onboard early sellers within the 25-authorization cap.

steps.title: List on the Selling Partner Appstore
steps.detail: Submit an Appstore listing to remove the authorization cap.

agentCanDo: Map operations to the minimum SP-API roles
Draft the developer profile and security answers
Implement the consent URL, state check and LWA token exchange
Build Restricted Data Token handling if PII is needed
Track token age and prompt annual reauthorization
humanMustDo: Register as the primary account user
Have the security team verify control answers
Attend the solution architect meeting for PII roles
Self-authorize test accounts in Seller Central

blockers.symptom: Can't create an app in the portal
blockers.cause: Developer profile hasn't been approved yet.
blockers.fix: Wait for the 1–2 week review, or fix the stated denial reason and resubmit.

blockers.cause: Unlisted public seller apps are capped at 25 OAuth authorizations.
blockers.fix: List the app on the Selling Partner Appstore.

blockers.symptom: Consent screen authorizes the published version, not your new draft
blockers.cause: version=beta was omitted from the consent URL.
blockers.fix: Add version=beta when testing a Draft app.

blockers.cause: spapi_oauth_code expired (5 minutes), redirect_uri mismatch, or the full flow exceeded 10 minutes.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code immediately with the registered redirect_uri; restart the flow from your site if needed.

blockers.symptom: Order buyer/shipping fields missing or 403 on PII operations
blockers.cause: No restricted role, or the call wasn't made with a Restricted Data Token.
blockers.fix: Get the restricted role approved, add it to the app, re-authorize sellers, and use an RDT.

blockers.symptom: Calls start failing a year after a seller connected
blockers.fix: Track authorization age and prompt sellers to reauthorize before it lapses.

nuances.text: LWA access tokens typically last 1 hour (expires_in 3600); refresh tokens are long-lived but sellers must reauthorize annually.
Adding a new role after launch requires relisting and getting new authorizations from each seller to mint a new refresh token.
Private apps are self-authorized only and capped at 10 self-authorizations — fine for your own seller account, not for customers.
Amazon's 2026 fee plan ($1,400/year plus $0.40 per 1,000 GET calls over quota) was postponed in March 2026 and reportedly cancelled 'at this time' on May 12, 2026.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Reported by Nova Analytics, a vendor; Amazon's announcement page returned 404 to us.

nuances.text: SP-API docs moved from developer-docs.amazon.com to developer-docs.amazon (301 redirect).
Some operations are grantless and don't need seller authorization; vendor apps authorize a group of vendor codes at once.
